new_value: Chapter III Sections 1-3 (classification, high-risk requirements, and obligations of providers, deployers and other parties, including the Art. 16(f) duty to undergo conformity assessment) apply from 2 December 2027 for AI systems classified high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, except Art. 6(5).
reason: Sections 1-3 do not contain the conformity assessment framework (that is Section 5, Arts 40-49); the gloss overstated what point (c) postpones.

new_value: Art 113 third para point (c)(i) as replaced by Reg 2026/1744 Art 1 point (40)(b). Section 5 (Arts 40-49: standards, conformity assessment, certificates, registration) is not listed in point (c); provider and deployer duties that trigger it (e.g. Art 16(f), Art 26) sit in Section 3 and are postponed.
Art. 113 (second para.) and (third para.) points (a), (b), (d), as amended by Reg. 2026/1744 Art 1 point (40)
reason: General application date 2 August 2026 is in the second paragraph; the first paragraph is entry into force.

new_value: Point (d) (Arts 102-110 from 27 July 2026) and the 2 Dec 2026 date for Art 5(1)(ba),(bb), 5(1a),(1b) are in the operative amended text. The general date does not apply to Chapter III Sections 1-3, postponed by point (c) to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) / 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I).
reason: Prevent misreading of the general date.

new_value: Art. 6(5); Art. 113, third para., point (c) (exception for Art. 6(5)), as amended

Technical documentation drawn up before market placement must contain at least the Annex IV elements, including (point 2(g)) validation and testing procedures, the data used and its main characteristics, metrics for accuracy, robustness and compliance, potentially discriminatory impacts, and dated, signed test logs and reports, and (point 4) a justification of the chosen performance metrics. SMEs and SMCs may use a simplified Commission form, which notified bodies must accept.
reason: Add the amended Art 11(1) second subpara (Reg 2026/1744 Art 1 point (10)) and the correct content of Annex IV point 4.

new_value: Art. 42(2); Art. 42(3) (inserted by Reg. 2026/1744 Art 1 point (18))

High-risk systems certified, or covered by a statement of conformity, under an EU cybersecurity scheme (Reg. 2019/881) whose references are published in the OJ are presumed to meet the Art. 15 cybersecurity requirements to the extent covered; systems within the scope of Reg. 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) are deemed to comply with the Art. 15 cybersecurity requirements where the conditions of Art. 12(1) of that Regulation are met.
reason: Add statement-of-conformity route and the precise CRA condition.
Presumption is used in pre-market conformity assessment; consistent with row 037.

new_value: The Commission may adopt common specifications by implementing act only if (a) it requested harmonised standards and the request was not accepted, the standards were not delivered on time, insufficiently address fundamental rights, or do not comply with the request, and (b) no reference to covering harmonised standards is published in the OJ or expected within a reasonable period; conformity with common specifications gives a presumption of conformity to the extent covered.
reason: Add the cumulative condition (b) and the fourth trigger.

new_value: Notified-body certificates are valid for the period stated, at most five years for Annex I systems and four years for Annex III systems, extendable at the provider's request after re-assessment; where a system no longer meets Section 2 requirements the body must, applying proportionality, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless the provider takes corrective action within the deadline set by the body.
reason: Add restriction option and corrective-action exception.

new_value: Before placing on the market or putting into service an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2, registered at national level), the provider registers itself and the system in the EU database; providers that conclude under Art. 6(3) that an Annex III system is not high-risk must also register; deployers that are public authorities or Union institutions/bodies (or act on their behalf) must register, select the system and register its use before putting it into service or using it.
reason: Cover Art 49(2), which the cited range includes; Art 49 not amended by Reg 2026/1744.
